passage.title: Antibiotic Resistance
passage.body: Antibiotics transformed medicine in the twentieth century, turning once-fatal infections into routine problems that a short course of tablets could cure. Today, that achievement is under threat. Bacteria reproduce so quickly that any mutation which helps a microbe survive a drug spreads through a population within days, and each time an antibiotic is used, susceptible bacteria are killed while resistant ones are left to multiply. The more often a drug is prescribed, therefore, the faster resistance to it develops. Overuse is not confined to hospitals. In several countries antibiotics are available without a prescription, and in agriculture they are routinely added to animal feed to promote growth. Patients also contribute when they stop taking a course as soon as they feel better, since the weakest bacteria die first and the hardier survivors remain. Researchers warn that the pipeline of new drugs is thin, largely because developing an antibiotic is expensive and offers pharmaceutical companies little profit compared with medicines taken every day for chronic conditions. Some health economists have therefore proposed that governments pay companies a fixed fee for new antibiotics, regardless of how many are sold, so that firms are rewarded for innovation rather than for volume. Such a scheme would only work, of course, if doctors used the new drugs sparingly.

items.definition: Antibiyotik direnci üzerine akademik bir metin ve beş okuduğunu anlama sorusu.

options: the history of antibiotics in twentieth-century medicine
the best way for patients to complete a course of tablets
the causes of antibiotic resistance and one proposed remedy
the profits that pharmaceutical companies earn from antibiotics
the use of antibiotics in agriculture
questions.explanationTR: Metin direncin nedenlerini sıralıyor ve sabit ücret önerisini tartışıyor: (C). (A) tarih yalnızca giriş cümlesidir. (B) hasta davranışı nedenlerden yalnızca biridir. (D) kâr, yeni ilaçların azlığının açıklamasıdır, ana konu değildir. (E) tarım, yalnızca bir örnektir ve konuyu fazla daraltır.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, resistance to a drug develops faster when ----.
options: the drug is prescribed more frequently
bacteria reproduce more slowly
patients complete every course of treatment
antibiotics are reserved for use in hospitals
new drugs enter the market more quickly
questions.explanationTR: «The more often a drug is prescribed, the faster resistance to it develops» cümlesi bunu doğrudan söyler: (A). (B) bakterilerin hızlı üremesi direncin nedenidir, yavaş üremesi değil. (C) kürü tamamlamak dirençle ilişkilendirilmez. (D) kullanımın hastanelerle sınırlı olmadığı belirtilir.

questions.prompt: All of the following are given as contributors to antibiotic overuse EXCEPT ----.
options: the sale of antibiotics without a prescription
the addition of antibiotics to animal feed
patients stopping a course as soon as they feel better
the use of expired stocks by pharmacies
the frequent prescription of the drugs
questions.explanationTR: Soru metinde verilmeyen seçeneği arıyor: eczanelerin son kullanma tarihi geçmiş stokları metinde hiç geçmez: (D). (A) reçetesiz satış, (B) hayvan yemine katma, (C) kürü erken bırakma ve (E) sık reçete yazımı metinde açıkça anılan katkılardır.

questions.prompt: The proposal of a fixed fee for new antibiotics is intended to ----.
options: make antibiotics cheaper for patients
reward companies for developing drugs rather than for selling large quantities
encourage doctors to prescribe the new drugs more often
remove the need for further research
raise the price of medicines for chronic conditions
questions.explanationTR: Metin, firmaların «hacim yerine yenilik için» ödüllendirilmesini amaçladığını söylüyor: (B). (A) hasta fiyatından söz edilmez. (C) tersine, yeni ilaçların idareli kullanılması gerekir. (D) araştırma ihtiyacını ortadan kaldırmaz, teşvik eder.

questions.prompt: The final sentence suggests that a fixed-fee scheme ----.
options: will certainly put an end to antibiotic resistance
would be cheaper than any other possible scheme
is unnecessary because antibiotics already sell well
has already been adopted by several governments
could fail if the new antibiotics were prescribed too freely
questions.explanationTR: Son cümle planın ancak doktorlar yeni ilaçları idareli kullanırsa işe yarayacağını söylüyor; yani serbest reçete planı boşa çıkarabilir: (E). (A) «kesinlikle» mutlaklığı metinde yoktur. (B) «herhangi bir başka plandan» kıyası yapılmaz. (C) ilaçların az kâr getirdiği söylenir. (D) plan hâlâ bir öneridir.
